pr_title: Remove stale devices automatically for Roborock
pr_body:

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.

The Roborock home_data_v2 endpoint will give all devices currently on the account. If a user removes a device, it will no longer show up in home_data_v2, and will then be removed from the integration.

This currently can only happen once on config entry load, as we do not get this information on every coordinator update.

issue_context.title: Roborock integration has no "delete device" option
issue_context.body:
### The problem

When a device has discovered and added to the integration, and you (for instance) sell the device or it breaks down and get's replaced you have no option to delete the obsolete device in the integration. Even though the device has been deleted from the Roborock app, the obsolete device is still visible in the integration and there appears to be no (easy) way to delete the device.

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2024.11.3

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

Roborock

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/roborock

<sub><sup>(message by IssueLinks)</sup></sub>
I think the integration needs to support `async_remove_config_entry_device` https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/device_registry_index/#removing-devices to allow deleting devices

I had expected this to have been implemented already. I have searched the source but could not find any mention of `async_remove_config_entry_device` so I guess it really is not implemented yet. It would be beneficial to have this supported though. I would have looked into this into doing this myself but alas I have hardly any proper skills in Python so I am no use at this area. Also, I am not sure if this is something that is already been worked on. I see in the documentation that there are some big plans for this integration...

The discussion here sounds accurate. For future reference when we implement this https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/core/integration-quality-scale/rules/stale-devices describes the best practices.

review_comments: Can you add a test where a device is returned from the API but fails with an unavailability error? I want to make sure its not removed. (I also am not sure the current behavior of ignoring the coordinator is correct, and want to revisit that, and just want to be defensive here)
I was actually wondering the same thing today. We should probably set up and just mark as unavailable and just retry rather than ignore it.
